title: OnSIP pricing, features, and add-ons: What you should know in 2026
summary: OnSIP's pricing looks simple, but add-ons and pay-as-you-go fees can add up fast. See what it really costs in 2026.
body_markdown:
OnSIP markets itself as a communication platform for businesses that need scalable phone service. But its pricing structure and add-on fees can catch businesses off guard and push monthly costs well beyond their initial budget. This article breaks down OnSIP’s pricing plans and available add-ons. It also touches on the hidden costs and alternatives businesses should consider before signing up.


##


**OnSIP business phone plans and pricing**


OnSIP offers two business phone plans: Unlimited and Basic. At first glance, Basic looks like the pricier option. But the comparison isn’t quite apples-to-apples once you factor in how each plan actually charges for usage.

### **OnSIP Unlimited plan**


**Pricing:** $18.95 per user per month, minimum of five users


**Best for:** Medium-sized businesses with higher call volumes


While the Unlimited plan includes more features than the Basic plan, outbound SMS is a pooled allowance split across every user on the account. Some teams may reach this limit quickly.


Here’s what else you get:


- **Calling.** Unlimited within the US and Canada.


- **SMS.** Free inbound SMS, 250 outbound messages per account per month.


- **Auto attendants.** Unlimited auto-attendant menus.


- **Call parking lots.** Place calls into temporary “parking spots” for other team members to pick up.


- **Enhanced music on hold.** Play a customized music station for callers while they wait in call queues.


### **OnSIP Basic plan**


**Pricing:** $49.95 per account per month


**Best for:** Businesses with small teams and low call volumes


The Basic plan includes access to OnSIP’s browser, mobile, and


[desktop apps](https://www.quo.com/blog/voip-for-pc/) . Users can make or receive calls from any device. But domestic calling and


[outbound SMS](https://www.quo.com/product/messaging) aren’t included in that flat $49.95 monthly fee. Both are billed on a pay-as-you-go basis, so costs can add up quickly for teams that call or text often. The Basic plan also has limits for accessing other specific features like call recording and ring groups.


Here’s how this breaks down:


- **Calling.** $0.032 per minute.


- **SMS.** Inbound is free; outbound is $0.01 per message.


- **Auto-attendants.** Option to include up to three phone menus before you have to pay extra.


- **Ring groups.** Three ring groups are included. Additional ring groups cost extra.


- **Call recording.**[Call recording](https://www.quo.com/product/call-recording) is user-based. You get one user per account, then you have to pay for additional seats.


- **Voicemail.** Five


[voicemail](https://www.quo.com/product/voicemail) boxes per account. Additional seats cost extra.

On top of its Base plan pricing, OnSIP offers a range of add-ons that could change your monthly bill. Some apply only if you’re on the Basic plan, while others apply regardless of which plan you choose. It’s worth reviewing both before you commit to a plan.

##


**OnSIP’s true costs: Fees you have to know about**


Beyond the sticker price of each plan and the standard add-ons, OnSIP has fee and usage-based charges that can catch you by surprise. Here’s what to watch for:


- **Outbound SMS.** On the Basic plan, you’ll be paying for every text message sent. If you go over your Unlimited plan’s monthly SMS allowance, you’ll be charged $0.01 per message for local numbers.


- **Toll-free SMS.** Messages sent from a toll-free number cost more at $0.39 per message.


- **International calling in their extended calling areas.** While standard calling areas go beyond just the US, extended calling areas aren’t available by default. To access extended calling areas, you’ll need to complete a request form. Once approved, you’re capped at 100 minutes per call and a $10 daily allowance, regardless of your plan.


- **Call recording.** The Basic plan includes one free user per account, but every additional user who needs recording access costs $4.95 per user per month.


- **Porting an existing number.** Bringing a number over from another provider costs $15 per number, on top of ongoing monthly fees.


- **VoIP phones.** Free phones are only included on the Unlimited plan, and only if you have at least five users.


- **Toll-free numbers.** New toll-free numbers cost $7 each and require an application form. OnSIP recommends applying for a


[toll-free number](https://www.quo.com/toll-free-numbers) directly through them. Porting one in means paying the porting fee on top of the number’s own cost.


##


**Things to keep in mind before choosing OnSIP**


Before committing to OnSIP, there are a few practical considerations:


1. **Keep track of your usage.** Businesses on the Basic plan need to watch their minutes and messages closely, since pay-as-you-go costs climb as call and text volume grows. Even the Unlimited plan isn’t fully unlimited: it’s capped at 250 messages per month before you’re charged a per-message rate.


2. **No free trial.** OnSIP doesn’t currently offer a free trial, making it harder to test the platform before committing. They used to offer a free plan, but they’ve since discontinued it.


3. **Upgrades can get costly.** Many Basic plan features, like voicemail and call recording, have limits and cost extra to scale. This and other add-ons may significantly increase your monthly costs.


4. **Low scores for the mobile app.** OnSIP’s mobile app holds just 2.5 stars on the Google Play Store and 2.4 stars on the App Store. Reviewers have flagged recurring crashes that led to dropped calls and dead air


And one user reported missing notifications for incoming calls in early 2025. If a caller doesn’t leave a voicemail, there’s no record of the call. That’s a sharp contrast to Quo, which holds the top spot for customer satisfaction on G2 and has more than 6,500 five-star reviews on the App Store.


5. **Collaboration is an issue.** OnSIP is designed primarily around one-on-one customer communication. It’s missing several features teams rely on for internal coordination, like shared contacts, group messaging, and contact notes.

### Priced for growing businesses

A company with a 10-person team might see OnSIP as the cheaper option at first glance since they’d pay $49.95 for all users versus $150 with Quo. But 10 people calling and messaging on an OnSIP Basic plan can get

Quo’s per-user pricing scales more predictably because you’re only paying for the seat, not messaging or calling. Your costs will grow with your headcount, not your call volume.


Quo’s Starter plan also includes access to features that OnSIP locks behind add-ons or leaves out entirely. You won’t have to pay extra for collaboration tools, voicemail transcription, or on-demand call recording. That gives growing businesses more built-in value from the start.

### Collaborate with your team

##


**Pros and cons of OnSIP pricing plans**


OnSIP may be a good solution for businesses with basic needs. But growing companies will need an[OnSIP alternative](https://www.quo.com/blog/onsip-alternatives/) . Here are the key pros and cons of OnSIP:


#### Pros


- Controllable costs. Per-account and pay-as-you-go pricing means you can keep your bill low as long as you actively monitor usage.
- Customizable. You choose which add-on features to include, so you don’t pay for capabilities you don’t need.
- Free SIP trunking. You’ll reduce operating costs since you don’t need to maintain physical phone lines or set up local numbers in every market you operate in.


#### Cons


- Poor team collaboration. The lack of group messaging and contact notes makes it harder for teams to coordinate internally. That can affect the customer experience.
- Costs can escalate. The more you call and text, the more you pay. High-volume teams will likely spend more than they would with other providers. And remember, adding capabilities to your plan can significantly increase your monthly bill.
- No built-in time-savers. OnSIP doesn’t offer call transcription, call summaries, or automated texting workflows. You’ll be missing out on features that can save your team time elsewhere.
